name: Citronelle
lede: Citronelle is a vivid greenish yellow from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, first recorded in 1928.

sections.title: A 1928 dictionary name
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* places Citronelle on plate 18, cell L2, first recorded in 1928 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system files the same block as a vivid greenish yellow [2]. The word echoes *citronella*, the lemon-scented grass and its oil, but the dictionary does not say the name was chosen for that reason, so the connection is undocumented here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[dijon]], [[dirty-yellow]], [[sulphur-yellow]] and [[oil-yellow]], at 4.1, 4.1, 4.9 and 4.4 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this exact match in only 6 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [4]. Four of the six are 1890s Kalighat paper paintings from India; one is a Sargent still life and one a Bonnard landscape [4]. The small count fits a saturated, high-value yellow-green that is rare in oil but common in flat, modern dye work [4]. The match is computed, not a pigment test [4].
